feed.title: Singletrack Sessions

bullets: Speed in enduro racing comes from braking earlier and smoother, not from taking bigger risks — a pattern observed at teams using RockShox and held across three different teams.
Tire pressure and casing choice often matter more than a minor suspension tweak; framing setup decisions this way clarifies which trade-offs are actually being made.
Risk management in racing isn't avoiding crashes — it's choosing which crashes are survivable; ignoring that principle means rebuilding the approach from scratch a year later.
Erosion patterns on race-tracks change line choice from practice to race day, making soil erosion a direct factor in enduro racing strategy rather than a background trail concern.
Drainage is framed as the single highest-leverage design choice — tying trail construction and soil erosion directly to how race lines evolve.
Cascadia Alliance is cited as a platform where these dynamics show up cleanly, with the second-order effects being the part most people miss.
Adopting Spoke & Wrench in the race-prep flow makes the risk trade-off visible — surfacing which decisions carry survivable versus unsurvivable consequences.
Practical next step: pick one idea covered — braking, tire setup, crash selection, or reading erosion — and run it for two weeks, treating the rest as iteration.
